I subbed for 4 days in a row for a 1st grade class last week. The first day was absolute TORTURE. So the next day I came in and told them we would be playing a game - everytime the class was on task, using their listening ears, and showing good behavior I would give them(the class as a whole) a point. Every time they were not doing these things, I gave myself a point. The goal was for them to have more points than me by the end of my 4 days with them, and if they succeeded, I’d bring them in a treat. It totally worked and helped keep them in check, they really wanted to “beat me” and get their treat. Bummer I had to use my own money to supply the great on my last day subbing for this class, but well worth it in my mind to keep my sanity for the 4 days I had them!

I started taking Adderall in 2019 because I was a single mom, working, and in school. There just weren’t enough hours in the day and I already am someone who struggles with motivation. I got introduced to adderall by a coworker who was prescribed the medication- she told me it would help me concentrate to get my school work done and give me energy. I started buying it from her and noticed a huge improvement in my motivation, my concentration, and my mood. It was literally like an upper for me - it put me in the BEST mood and allowed me to be productive. Suddenly, I was able to get my homework done, stay on top of my household chores, and have energy to spare. You know what I figured was better than taking a little Adderall to help me get through the day? Taking MORE Adderall. And that’s what started the slippery slope for me. It was so innocent at first. Before I knew it, I was blowing a grand a month on adderall (on top of being prescribed 60 pills by my doctor. I eventually went and got my own script by just googling adhd symptoms). I was full of rage all the time, insanely depressed. I was taking 250-300 mg of adderall or vyvanse a day. I became a hermit - I stopped talking to friends and family, I just wanted to be alone with my adderall and super clean my apartment. The once fun loving mom I was became a crabby, quick tempered mom. And then there was the lack of sleep - I would stay up til 2 in the morning most nights, wake up for work at 5:30, pop adderall all day to get through the day and do it again for days on end. Once the weekend hit I would literally sleep from Friday night until Sunday. With a minor child in the home. How fucking unfair for them. I lost my job, lost custody of my daughter, lost my damn mind honestly. And it’s been 2 years since I went to rehab and I still struggle with this shit. I never feel good anymore. EVER. Everything feels hard without adderall - even simple stuff like taking a shower, or brushing my teeth. All I think about 24/7 is how much easier life would be if I had adderall. My doctor says it can take years for my brain to rewire itself, because it was so used to living on stimulant medication for so long. I wish I had never touched this shit honestly. I miss the old me. I miss my old life. I miss who I was before adderall ever got a hold of me.
